# implement.py drive: a driven child strays into another work item's worktree when its first finish gate is red

## Problem statement

When a driven child's first `finish` gate is red for a reason the child did not
introduce (a pre-existing environment-only failure), the child is expected to
stop after triage — but nothing currently stops it from going one step further:
creating a work item for the failure and **starting that item's implementation
itself**, inside a sibling worktree. The existing worktree-placement guard only
detects work that landed in the **main checkout**, so a driven child that
`cd`s into a different linked worktree is invisible to the guard, can race the
session that owns that worktree, silently widen the epic's scope, and consume
the host's test slots.

## Users

- **Implement-skill maintainer** — wants the placement guard to cover every
  linked worktree, not just the main checkout, so a driven child that writes
  into a sibling worktree is detected and refused with an actionable message.
- **Producer/operator running `/skill:implement <epic>`** — wants a drive that
  fails closed with both roots named when a child strays, instead of silently
  editing another item's tree or wedging the epic.
- **Driven child agent** — needs explicit guidance that a red first `finish`
  gate caused by a failure it did not introduce ends with triage and report,
  never with starting that failure's own implementation.

Example user stories:

- As an implement-skill maintainer, I want a driven child that edits another
  linked worktree to be detected by `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` and the run
  to fail closed with an actionable message naming both roots, so isolation
  between concurrent worktrees holds.
- As a producer driving an epic, I want a child whose `finish` gate is red
  because of a pre-existing failure to report the triage work item and stop —
  not begin implementing it in a sibling worktree that another session owns.
- As an agent working a driven child, I want a deterministic rule: a red gate
  I did not cause → triage (create work item) → report → stop.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child refuses (or is refused) any write whose path resolves into a
  linked worktree other than `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, with an actionable
  message naming both roots.
- A child whose `finish` gate is red because of a failure it did not introduce
  reports and stops (triage → work item), instead of starting that work item's
  implementation itself.
- Regression test: a simulated driven child that `cd`s into a sibling worktree
  is detected and the run fails closed (no status mutation of either item).
- The standard finish gate (`_worktree_placement_violation`) and the parent/
  drive placement guard (`_child_main_checkout_violation`) both treat changes
  in a **registered sibling worktree** of the same repository as a placement
  violation when the child's own worktree holds no work (precise-guard rule:
  unrelated dirt never blocks).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` blocker guidance
  (confined to driven sessions), and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A driven epic run can no longer be silently derailed: a child whose first
`finish` gate is red stops after triage, and a child that edits another item's
worktree is caught and the run fails closed naming both roots.

## Constraints

- **Do not change driven behaviour otherwise.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`
  semantics, driver-side worktree removal and the drive sweep stay exactly as
  they are (parent epic SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9, SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR).
- **Precision over false positives.** The guard fires only when the child's own
  worktree holds NO work (no dirty files, no commits ahead of the parent
  branch) while another change surface (main checkout or a sibling worktree)
  holds changes. Pre-existing/unrelated dirt never blocks a legitimate finish
  or a child whose work lives in its own worktree.
- **Sibling worktree = registered linked worktree** of the same repository
  (via `_registered_worktree_paths`), excluding the main checkout and the
  child's own worktree. A foreign repository checkout — even one reachable by
  path — is never treated as the child's write surface (cross-checkout
  attribution, SA-0MVXVBZF2009HRRN).
- **No status mutation on refusal.** A fail-closed placement refusal must not
  mutate either item's status; it reports (comment + structured report fields)
  and stops the chain, mirroring `_fail_placement`.
- **Do not invent a partial-overlap duplicate.** The completed item
  SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM ("cwd is not enough") covers main-checkout writes only;
  this item extends the guard to sibling worktrees and adds the red-gate stop
  rule. It is not a duplicate.
- **Built, tested, committed in a worktree** per the mandatory worktree
  requirement; never commit from the main checkout.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `_child_main_checkout_violation(child_id, worktree_path, parent_branch, repo_root)`
    (~line 18527) — post-hoc guard called from `phase_parent`'s two
    change-surface call sites (~14590, ~14650); fails the chain via
    `_fail_placement` (~14398) when a non-terminal child's worktree holds no
    work while the **main checkout** is dirty.
  - `_worktree_placement_violation(worktree_path, cwd, repo_root, parent_branch)`
    (~line 18428) — the `finish`-phase Step 0.5 gate; refuses when cwd is
    outside the worktree and main checkout holds changes while the worktree has
    none.
  - `_registered_worktree_paths(repo_root)` (~line 7188) — enumerates the
    worktrees git registers for a repo (already used to confine removal
    surfaces); this is the natural enumerator for sibling detection.
  - `_child_session_env()` (~14834) — injects `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` into
    the driven child's environment; `_child_main_checkout_violation` already
    names it as the contract the child must honour.
  - Drive loop `finish`-failure handling (~17620+) — the exact point where a
    red first gate is observed; the child-level instruction is what currently
    lets the child decide to implement the triaged item itself.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` line 11: "If you discover a blocker, create a new
  work-item, record the blocking relationship, and start working on it." The
  incident child followed this rule verbatim — which is exactly the behaviour
  AC2 must confine (driven sessions: triage and stop, do not start the new
  item).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` § Step 5 worktree requirement — `cwd` is not
  sufficient; `test "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" = "$IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH"`
  guard snippet already taught.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the placement-guard contract document;
  must be updated for the sibling-worktree extension.
- Tests: `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py`
  (`TestPlacementGuardContract`), `test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py`,
  `test_drive_child_session.py`.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the placement guard to sibling worktrees.** Teach
   `_child_main_checkout_violation` (and/or a new sibling-aware sibling)
   to enumerate `_registered_worktree_paths(repo_root)`, and — when the
   child's own worktree has no work — report a violation for any *other*
   registered linked worktree that holds changes, with an actionable message
   naming both roots (`IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` vs the offending sibling).
   Keep the finish-phase `_worktree_placement_violation` precise and
   symmetric where cwd/resolution indicates a sibling write.
2. **Red-gate stop rule for driven children.** Update
   `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`'s blocker guidance (or the driven-session instruction
   surface) so a driven child whose first `finish` gate is red for a failure
   it did not introduce: triages (creates a work item, records the blocking
   relationship) and **stops** — it does not run `implement.py start` for that
   item and does not edit its worktree. The drive loop already bounds retries;
   the behavioural fix is the instruction + the guard in (1) as the backstop.
3. **Regression tests.** Simulate a driven child that `cd`s into a sibling
   worktree (built with `git_sandbox` worktrees) and writes there; assert
   detection, fail-closed chain stop, and that neither item's status mutated.

## Risks & assumptions

- **False positives on legitimate sibling work.** A sibling worktree may hold
  another (non-driven) session's in-progress changes. Mitigation: the guard
  fires only when the child's own worktree has no work AND the sibling holds
  changes — plus the per-child lock probe (`_probe_child_lock`) can
  distinguish a live owner; an actively-held sibling is reported, not blamed.
- **The red-gate stop rule is instruction-level, so a misbehaving agent can
  ignore it.** Mitigation: the extended placement guard in AC1 is the
  mechanical backstop — even if a child tries to implement the triaged item,
  writing into a sibling worktree fails closed.
- **Wordiness of scope** — the drive's finish-retry/reconcile machinery must
  not be reworked; scope is the placement guard + the behavioural rule +
  regression tests. Extra opportunities (e.g. a session-level write guard)
  are recorded as linked work items, not folded in.
- **Documentation divergence** — SKILL.md, AGENTS_GLOBAL.md and
  worktree-isolation.md must stay consistent with the new guard; covered by
  the docs AC.
- Assumption: a "sibling worktree" is any path listed by
  `_registered_worktree_paths` other than the main checkout and the child's
  own worktree — a foreign repo checkout is never in scope.
- Assumption: `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` remains the single source of truth
  for the driven child's worktree root; no new env var is introduced.

## Key Files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — extend `_child_main_checkout_violation`
  / `_worktree_placement_violation` for sibling worktrees; add sibling-worktree
  offending-path detection beside `_main_checkout_offending_paths`; message
  naming both roots.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py` — extend
  `TestPlacementGuardContract` with sibling-worktree cases (dirty sibling,
  clean sibling, own-worktree-has-work exemption).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py` or a new
  drive regression test — simulated driven child `cd`s into a sibling worktree;
  fail-closed run; no status mutation of either item.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — driven-child red-gate rule (Step 5 / driven
  session guidance).
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — confine the "discover a blocker → start working on it"
  rule for driven sessions (triage and stop).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — document the sibling-worktree guard and
  the red-gate stop rule.

## Related work

- SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM — "Enforce and document that driven child sessions must
  work inside their worktree (cwd is not enough)" (completed): the existing
  main-checkout guard this item extends. Partial overlap — the ACs here cover
  the sibling-worktree gap and the red-gate stop; not a duplicate.
- SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM — "Implement skill safety gate should account for git
  worktrees" (completed): safety-gate ancestry; the guard's precision rules
  (expected-dirty paths, per-worktree dirt) are reused here.
- SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9 — "implement skill: drive all epic children to
  completion (fresh session per child)" (completed): the drive feature whose
  driven-child semantics must not change.
- SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR — "implement.py finish removes the worktree under a
  driven child session, wedging it" (completed): driven-child worktree
  ownership; sibling detection must not disturb removal ownership.
- SA-0MVLJXVND0015LPW / SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL — drive reset / finish-attempt
  bound (completed): the retry machinery around the red-gate path.
- SA-0MVXVBZF2009HRRN — "Regression tests: cross-checkout attribution"
  (completed): a sibling repository is never the write surface.
- SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR / SA-0MW7LMUUQ00701KJ — driven-child lock ownership
  (completed): the per-child lock that a stray child must not race.
- WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG (ContextHub) — the epic that was driven when the
  incident occurred (discovery source).
- WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN — the pre-existing environment-only test failure
  (hyphenated TMPDIR) tracked alongside this incident.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Auto-dispatched intake (herdr downtime worker) — no interactive interview
round. No questions were asked of the operator in this session.

- Q: "Should the sibling-worktree guard be post-hoc detection or a live
  write-intercept?" — Answer (assumed, documented): **post-hoc detection**,
  consistent with the existing `_child_main_checkout_violation` /
  `_worktree_placement_violation` architecture and AC3's wording ("is detected
  and the run fails closed"). Research: both existing guards are post-hoc and
  fail closed at `phase_parent`/`phase_drive`/`finish`; there is no
  write-intercept layer to hook. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer/plan review:
  confirm post-hoc detection is sufficient (Recommended), rather than adding a
  session-level write guard.
- Q: "Where does the red-gate stop rule live?" — Answer (assumed,
  documented): instruction-level change in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`/SKILL.md driven
  guidance (triage and stop, never start the new item), with the extended
  placement guard from AC1 as the mechanical backstop. Research: the incident
  child followed the AGENTS.md blocker rule verbatim; the drive loop already
  bounds finish retries, so no new driver-side machinery is needed beyond the
  guard. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer/plan review: is confining the blocker
  rule to driven sessions the right scope, versus a global behavioural change?
- Research summary: inspected `implement.py` placement guards (`_child_main_checkout_violation`,
  `_worktree_placement_violation`, `_registered_worktree_paths`,
  `_fail_placement`, `_child_session_env`), the drive loop finish-failure
  handling, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` blocker guidance, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
  worktree section and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`; searched the worklog
  for related drive/worktree/guard items (20+ matches reviewed). No full
  duplicate found; SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM is the closest completed ancestor and
  is explicitly linked as partial overlap.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVXVESFB002IQ9I** – Close coverage gap: **Cross-checkout safety.** A command run inside one checkout (worktree or repo) can never delete ... (completed)
- **SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V** – Unify test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout (open)
- **SA-0MWCQT1TQ0028E6D** – Recover guarded-child delegation guard (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvte8xaj002iudr, 0mvxwmvth007mnjr, 0mw7lmuuq00701kj, ac1, ac2 (+370 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance, account (+359 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0muwnhkqh0034dw9, 0mvljxs7r000xifl, 0mvljxvnd0015lpw, 0mvte8xaj002iudr, 0mw7lmuuq00701kj (+358 more)

# Gate frame fallback: framed vitest runs are never unparsed

## Goal

Guard the gate classification path so a non-zero vitest run carrying a
`❯ <file>:<line>:<col>` frame is **never** classified `unparsed`/
infrastructure — even when no structured failure record could be built
(SA-0MW0NL3EW0009R4G AC6). When `failures` is empty but the bounded
stderr/stdout tail contains a vitest frame, classify `test_failure` and report
the frame as the failing location.

Lives in the gate classification path used by `implement.py finish` and the
pre-push hook: `implement.py::_gate_failure_kind` and/or the shared
`test/scripts/gate_reason.py::classify_gate_result` (single shared classifier,
SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI). Consults the already-carried bounded `stdout`/`stderr`
tails (`_adapt_guarded_result`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A non-zero vitest run with a `❯ <file>:<line>:<col>` frame is never classified `unparsed`/infrastructure: the frame is reported as the failing location even when no structured failure record can be built (empty `failures` list), proven by a gate-classification test.
- The operator-facing gate detail/message reports the frame as the failing location in that case.
- A genuinely unparsable non-zero run still falls back to `unparsed`/`killed` as today: a frame-less, marker-less non-zero gate result still classifies `unparsed` (no regression; ENOSPC control).
- A signal-killed run whose tail happens to contain a frame still classifies `killed` — the frame fallback replaces only the `unparsed` outcome, never `killed`/`timeout`/`slot_contention`/`infrastructure`.

**Key Files:**
- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py
- skill/test/scripts/gate_reason.py


## Impact

A red vitest test push now names the failing file and line from the frame in the gate's output tail instead of blaming the command or configuration, so an operator is never sent hunting for an infrastructure fault after a genuine test failure.
data.title: Gate frame fallback: framed vitest runs are never unparsed

# Document vitest frame parsing and tail-window handling

## Goal

Update the skill reference docs so operators know exactly which vitest output
shapes are parsed and why a `FAIL` header trimmed away by the 1200-char gate
tail is no longer fatal (SA-0MW0NL3EW0009R4G AC4/AC8).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) states which reporters are parsed — including the frame-only `❯ <file>:<line>:<col>` shape (optional project pipe and node-mode `FAIL` header) in the Failure parsing table.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` states the tail-window rationale: the tail window is documented as sufficient because the frame parser no longer needs the `FAIL` header (captured-tail handling).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` states the gate's frame fallback: a non-zero vitest run with a frame in the tail is `test_failure`, never `unparsed`.
- Every claim in both docs matches the parser's and gate's actual behaviour (no stale statements about which reporters are parsed).

**Key Files:**
- docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md
- docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md

## Impact

Operators and agents reading the skill references now see exactly which Vitest
output shapes are parsed as structured failures — including the tail-trimmed
`❯ <file>:<line>:<col>` frame — and why the 1200-character gate tail is
sufficient, so a real browser/unit failure is never mistaken for an
infrastructure problem.
data.title: Document vitest frame parsing and tail-window handling
